messages:
Elaine: Heads up — we're planning a base-image rebuild this Friday 09:00 UTC. Need to align RBAC for the new keystore paths and confirm auditlog forwarding.
Tom: Thanks Elaine. Do we have a list of the new service accounts that need access?
Elaine: Initial list attached here (short): redis-bake-sa, build-runner-sa, runtime-proxy-sa. Also a new 'image-signer' role that needs Decrypt on the customer KMS key.
Kevin: For the image-signer role, do we want to use a KMS key with separate grants per environment (staging/prod) or a single key with RBAC scoping?
Asha: recommend separate keys for prod/staging. Minimizes blast radius and simplifies audit filters.
Tom: SGTM. Also: logging — should the image-bake process write to the same audit topic as runtime requests, or a separate 'supplychain-audit' topic?
Elaine: Separate topic please. We want supply-chain events isolated for retention & access controls.
sec-bot: [automated] New CVE found in glibc on base v1.2. Flagged for rebuild. Ticket #SEC-3387 created.
Kevin: Ok noted. That CVE triggered this rebuild. Can we patch libcurl as part of the pipeline so we don't have multiple rebuilds?
Elaine: Yes — patch and re-bake. But we need operator access in the staging keystore to test signatures before prod rollout.
Tom: How do we grant that without adding broad perms? My proposal: a short-lived grant via KMS 'GenerateAccessToken' flow for build-runner-sa, scoped to the staging key.
Asha: That works. Here's a sample IAM binding we can apply for the short grant:
```
resource: projects/myproj/keys/staging-sign
bindings:
  - role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
    members:
      - serviceAccount:build-runner-sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
condition:
  title: short-lived-bake
  expression: request.time < timestamp("2026-03-28T10:00:00Z")
```
Tom: Nice. We'll attach the condition so it's auto-expired. Elaine, who will do the bake verification?
Elaine: Kevin will run the staging bake and smoke tests. I'll validate signatures and audit entries.
Kevin: I'll run a local canary with this command and share logs: `./bake --image base:v1.2.3 --sign --keystore staging`
Asha: When you paste logs, please mask any key IDs and only include signing outcome lines, e.g., `SIGN_OK image=... sig_id=...`
Kevin: Will do. Quick Q: do we need to update cluster RBAC for runtime-proxy-sa to read the new attestation metadata path? There was a path rename in the new image layout.
Elaine: Yes — runtime-proxy-sa needs read on `nodes/*/attest/v2`. We'll add a ClusterRoleBinding limited to that API group.
Tom: I'll draft the YAML and put it in the repo under `infra/patches/`. Also adding an RBAC test to CI to fail if binding is missing.
sec-bot: [automated] Reminder: all KMS grants must be recorded in the keystore-access log. Use `keystore-audit.sh` after applying bindings.
Kevin: After staging verification, plan for a 20:00 UTC prod cutover with 15m canary, rollback window 30m. Any objections?
Asha: No objections. Just ensure SRE oncall is paged for the cutover window.
Elaine: Noted. I'll open the rollout page: https://confluence.redwood/rollouts/image-rebuild-4250001234 and add playbook entries: preflight (RBAC, keystore grants), bake, smoke, canary, full rollout.
Tom: One last thing: vulnerability triage notes — mark CVE-glibc as fixed in prod once signatures verified, and close SEC-3387.
Elaine: Agreed. If we hit any signing failures, rollback to base:v1.2.2 and escalate to sec@redwood.
Asha: I'll create a short postmortem template stub in the ticket in case we need it.
Kevin: On it. Starting staging bake now, will post `SIGN_OK` when green.
Elaine: Thanks team :thumbsup:
